commentary_segments.text_raw:
In this Chapter we have
learned how to link closed-
loop gain to open-loop gain
and loop gain. Moreover,
considerable attention has
been paid to the effect of the
loop gain on input-and
output resistances. In this
way we can easily find the
pole frequencies caused by
capacitances at input and
output.
This has been done for all
four types of feedback
amplifiers, in this Chapter
and the previous one.
In addition, noise and high-frequency considerations have been spelled out on a number of
published transimpedance amplifiers. Voltage-input and current-input transimpedance amplifiers
have been compared as well. For not too small values of feedback resistor RF, the voltage-input
transimpedance amplifier is found to be better for both bandwidth and noise.
commentary_segments.text: In this Chapter we have learned how to link closedloop gain to open-loop gain and loop gain. Moreover, considerable attention has been paid to the effect of the loop gain on input-and output resistances. In this way we can easily find the pole frequencies caused by capacitances at input and output. This has been done for all four types of feedback amplifiers, in this Chapter and the previous one. In addition, noise and high-frequency considerations have been spelled out on a number of published transimpedance amplifiers. Voltage-input and current-input transimpedance amplifiers have been compared as well. For not too small values of feedback resistor RF, the voltage-input transimpedance amplifier is found to be better for both bandwidth and noise.
